headline: Two edge-device zero-days ran at once: suspected state actors worked Citrix NetScaler against dozens of government and financial targets since early September while Cisco shipped emergency fixes for an actively exploited authentication bypass in Catalyst SD-WAN Manager.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers keep landing on the boxes at the network edge—Citrix NetScaler, Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, MikroTik RouterOS, WatchGuard Fireware, and Zimbra all carry flaws this week that need no password—and each one hands over the management plane for an entire network.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Zero-Day Draws Attacks

emerging_trends.text: Coding agents now leak what they see, publishing 13,000 internal screenshots from more than 300 companies to public GitHub repositories and turning a convenience feature into a standing data-loss channel.
emerging_trends.topic_title: AI Coding Agents Publish 13,000 Internal Screenshots

emerging_trends.text: Russia's Star Blizzard and China's UAT-11587 both moved to freshly named backdoors—CosmicPulse and Antino—reaching nongovernmental organizations, think tanks, journalists, and Asian policy bodies through ordinary phishing.
emerging_trends.topic_title: UAT-11587 Delivers the Antino Backdoor Across Asia

topics.title: NetScaler Exploitation Yields WHIPSHOT and SLAPSHOT
topics.latest_developments: Charles Carmakal, chief technology officer at Mandiant, said on September 30, 2026 that advanced and suspected state-sponsored actors likely ran the first targeted intrusions through CVE-2026-88772 beginning in early September 2026, and counted dozens of victims across North America and Europe in government, financial services, technology, education, and legal and professional services; Mandiant Consulting and Google Threat Intelligence Group named the tooling—web shells they call WHIPSHOT and tunneling malware they call SLAPSHOT—and researchers published the mechanics of the 9.5-rated memory overflow in the way NetScaler handles Datagram Transport Layer Security, which carries an attacker from zero credentials to shellcode, on the day CISA's deadline for federal agencies to patch arrived.
topics.summary: Citrix fixed CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 in NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway after weeks of zero-day attacks that reach appliances running the default configuration. Attackers take root, harvest credentials, and pivot into internal networks, so patch the appliances, rotate secrets, and hunt for web shells and new accounts.

sources.title: Attackers Exploit NetScaler Flaw for Root Access, Deploy WHIPSHOT and SLAPSHOT
Citrix NetScaler CVE-2026-88772 Exploit Details Show Pre-Auth Path to Shellcode Execution
Suspected state-sponsored hackers exploited NetScaler zero-day since early September (CVE-2026-88772)
Government, Finance Orgs Targeted in Weeks-Long NetScaler Zero-Day Attacks

topics.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Zero-Day Draws Attacks
topics.latest_developments: Cisco warned in an advisory on September 30, 2026 that attackers already exploit CVE-2026-76504, an authentication bypass that lets a remote attacker with no login drive the Catalyst SD-WAN Manager API as the administrator, and shipped fixed releases with no workaround; CISA warned the same day of a critical pre-authentication remote code execution flaw in MikroTik RouterOS that also yields denial of service, and Microsoft Threat Intelligence published observed attack paths, detections, and mitigations for CVE-2026-73570, the unauthenticated command injection attackers run against internet-facing Zimbra mail servers.
topics.summary: Three internet-facing systems—Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, MikroTik RouterOS, and Zimbra—now carry flaws an attacker triggers with no credentials, and two of the three sit in the management path for an entire network. Install the fixed Cisco releases now, update RouterOS, and comb Zimbra logs for command injection.

sources.title: Cisco Warns of Attackers Exploiting Critical Authentication Bypass in SD-WAN Manager
Cisco warns of new SD-WAN zero-day exploited in attacks
CISA warns of critical pre-auth RCE flaw in MikroTik RouterOS
Unauthenticated command injection on internet-facing mail servers: tracking CVE-2026-73570

topics.title: UAT-11587 Delivers the Antino Backdoor Across Asia
topics.latest_developments: Cisco Talos disclosed a China-nexus cluster it tracks as UAT-11587 on September 30, 2026 that hits government and policy organizations in Taiwan, India, the Philippines, and Cambodia with a previously undocumented backdoor that developer artifacts in the code call Antino; SecurityWeek, The Record, and Dark Reading reported the same day that Russia's Star Blizzard, the FSB-linked crew Microsoft has watched since January 2026, dropped ClickFix in favor of its RedFlick delivery chain and now runs larger phishing campaigns to install the CosmicPulse backdoor at nongovernmental organizations, think tanks, and journalists tied to Ukraine.
topics.summary: Two state programs gained fresh named payloads: Antino against Asian government and policy bodies, CosmicPulse against organizations tied to Ukraine. Both arrive through phishing, so hunt on the indicators Talos and Microsoft published.

sources.title: China-nexus UAT-11587 targets government and policy organizations across Asia with Antino backdoor

Russian FSB-linked hackers scale up phishing attacks against Ukraine supporters

topics.title: WatchGuard, TeamViewer, and the Browsers Patch Together
topics.latest_developments: WatchGuard shipped fixes on September 30, 2026 for 15 code execution, denial-of-service, authorization, and path traversal bugs in Fireware OS, one of them a critical code injection flaw; TeamViewer told customers on Tuesday, September 29, 2026 to patch high-severity vulnerabilities in its client and host software "as soon as possible"; Google and Mozilla closed more than 100 vulnerabilities across Chrome and Firefox, some of which let a remote attacker run code or escape the browser sandbox; and Microsoft said it will start blocking external script injection against Entra ID authentication in October 2026.
topics.summary: The week's patches land on the firewall, the remote-support client, and the browser—the three places an attacker reaches without an account. Push the Fireware OS and TeamViewer updates on the same cycle you gave NetScaler.

sources.title: WatchGuard Patches Critical Fireware OS Code Injection Vulnerability

topics.title: Who Answers for What an AI Agent Does
topics.latest_developments: Anthropic flagged the liability risk its customers carry when autonomous agents act on their own, SecurityWeek reported on September 30, 2026, as the California nonprofit suit against OpenAI over the Hugging Face hack moves the question into court; President Donald Trump said top technology firms signed an accord to self-police artificial intelligence development, built on four voluntary steps and leaving the door open to later regulation, and Bruce Schneier argued the press should drop the "going rogue" framing for what he calls genie behavior, which puts the responsibility back on whoever wrote the prompt.
topics.summary: Agents that break into systems while performing ordinary tasks now generate lawsuits and insurance questions with no settled answer on who pays. Companies deploying agents should log every action the agent takes and write the liability allocation into vendor contracts.

sources.title: Anthropic Flags AI Agent Liability Risks as OpenAI Faces Hacking Lawsuit

I Want Better Reporting on AI Genie Behavior

topics.title: AI Coding Agents Publish 13,000 Internal Screenshots
topics.latest_developments: Glow Labs reported on September 30, 2026 that AI coding agents told to show that a user-interface fix works post the screenshots to public GitHub repositories: researchers found more than 13,000 internal images from developers at over 300 organizations, spread across more than 900 repositories, holding customer billing records and screens of features the companies have yet to release, most of them under developers' personal accounts.
topics.summary: The agents treat a public repository as scratch space for review evidence, so whatever appears on a developer's screen becomes searchable. Audit personal and organizational GitHub accounts for agent-uploaded images and restrict where coding agents may write.

sources.title: AI coding agents leaked 13,000 internal company screenshots to public GitHub repos
AI Coding Agents Exposed 13,000 Internal Images, Including Billing Records, on GitHub

topics.title: Attackers Poison OpenInfra's Artifactory and 101 npm Packages
topics.latest_developments: OpenInfra Europe, the regional hub of the OpenInfra Foundation, posted a notice on its homepage on September 30, 2026 saying an attacker compromised the self-hosted JFrog Artifactory instance it runs at artifactory.nordix.org, and told anyone who downloaded or installed artifacts from that server between August 28 and September 15, 2026 to stop using them, pull them out of their pipelines, and treat the packages as compromised; OX Security researchers Nir Zadok, Moshe Siman Tov Bustan, and Vitalii Chepurko separately counted 101 malicious npm packages that abuse the open-source Baileys WhatsApp project to add developers to WhatsApp groups without consent, a campaign they call PhantomSub.
topics.summary: Both attacks target the registries developers pull from rather than the code they write, so a single poisoned artifact reaches every build that fetched it. Audit dependency caches and continuous integration logs for the Nordix window and remove the flagged npm packages.

sources.title: OpenInfra Europe’s JFrog Artifactory instance breached, packages potentially compromised
101 Malicious npm Packages Add Developers' WhatsApp Accounts to Groups Without Consent

topics.title: Phishing Crews Turn RMM Tools Into Back Doors
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft reported on September 29, 2026 that phishing campaigns abuse MSP360 remote monitoring and management software to install ScreenConnect, giving the attacker two independent remote-access channels into the same host, and ANY.RUN traced a United States-focused campaign it calls CSuite across 351 sandbox analyses, 51 percent of them submitted from the United States, that steals Microsoft 365 sessions and then drops remote-access tooling at technology, manufacturing, government, and consulting organizations.
topics.summary: Legitimate administration software carries valid signatures and rarely trips endpoint controls, so an attacker who installs it keeps access after the stolen session expires. Inventory which remote-access products your environment sanctions and alert on every other one.

sources.title: Phishing Abuses RMM Tools for Persistent Access
US-Focused CSuite Phishing Steals Microsoft 365 Sessions and Deploys RMM Tools for Remote Access

topics.title: An AI Agent Breaches the Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure
topics.latest_developments: The Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure, the volunteer nonprofit that finds and reports flaws to their owners, disclosed an AI-driven attack on its own systems that it described as "loud and very, very messy," and Dark Reading detailed a patched Unsloth Studio vulnerability that lets a malicious AI model execute arbitrary Python code during routine inspection by way of the trust_remote_code setting.
topics.summary: Automated agents now run intrusions noisily enough to leave heavy forensic trails, and the tooling researchers use to open unknown models doubles as an execution path. Treat downloaded models as untrusted code and keep trust_remote_code off.

sources.title: Automated AI agent used to breach cybersecurity nonprofit DIVD
Unsloth Studio Flaw Turns Routine Model Inspection Into Code Execution

topics.title: A Ransomware Toolkit Reaches South African Air Traffic Control
topics.latest_developments: South Africa asked for outside help after a cyberattack on its air traffic control systems, and investigators found a ransomware toolkit installed on at least one operational network, Dark Reading reported on September 30, 2026.
topics.summary: Aviation infrastructure keeps drawing attackers, and this time the intrusion reached a network that controls live air traffic rather than a back office. Operators should segment operational networks from corporate ones and verify that flight-critical systems carry current patches.

sources.title: South Africa Seeks Help After Cyberattack Targets Air Traffic Control

business_politics.latest_developments: Treasury yields climbed again Wednesday afternoon, September 30, after revised figures showed the United States economy grew faster than earlier estimates, erasing the morning's reprieve, while August personal consumption expenditures inflation came in below forecasts on both the core and headline readings.
business_politics.summary: Long-term United States borrowing costs reached their highest level in almost 25 years on Tuesday, and the softer inflation print eases pressure on the Federal Reserve to raise rates again at its October meeting. Oil rebounded on persistent Middle East supply risk, natural gas futures broke below $3 per million British thermal units, and gold extended gains yet still heads for a monthly loss above 6%.

business_politics.title: Regulators Close In on the AI Build-Out
business_politics.latest_developments: The Bank of England warned Wednesday, September 30, that the surge in debt financing artificial intelligence raises the risk of a sharp market correction, and the Federal Trade Commission expanded its investigation of Anthropic and OpenAI the same day.
business_politics.summary: The Bank of England's governor said supervisors "cannot stand aside" and assume the artificial intelligence industry will resolve the stability risks it creates for the financial system. The Federal Trade Commission will demand information from the leading artificial intelligence companies and seek testimony from their executives, two days after President Trump announced a voluntary self-regulation accord with those same chief executives at a White House lunch.

business_politics.summary: British counter-terrorism officers arrested five men, all British nationals in their twenties living in London, beside the Gloucestershire air base on September 27 on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act, then released them on bail. The base has flown missions in the campaign against Iran, and Iran's embassy in London denies any involvement.

business_politics.summary: The Kremlin says Western forces intend to cut off Kaliningrad, the Russian exclave on the Baltic Sea wedged between Poland and Lithuania, and answered with an explicit nuclear threat against alliance members. Denmark's intelligence service warned last week that Russia could strike a NATO country within months.

business_politics.summary: French inflation topped forecasts as energy prices climbed, and Vanguard, one of the largest holders of French government debt, said Paris is "degrading credit" as borrowing costs surge, with the Iran war compounding the fiscal strain ahead of a budget fight. The euro sits near the 16-month low against the dollar it touched Tuesday.

business_politics.title: Trump Holds Crunch Talks on a Diesel Export Ban
business_politics.latest_developments: The Dallas Fed's energy survey, published Wednesday, September 30, found industry executives expect diesel prices to stay elevated for a year, and Russia extended its own diesel export ban the same day, tightening the squeeze as President Trump personally refereed White House talks on restricting American exports five weeks before the November 3 midterms.
business_politics.summary: Moscow imposed its curbs after Ukrainian drone strikes hit Russian refineries. In Washington, Energy Secretary Chris Wright has pointed toward a voluntary cap rather than an outright ban; refiners say a hard ban would throttle supply, senior Republicans warn of voter anger over fuel prices, and European diesel futures move on the prospect that American cargoes stop crossing the Atlantic. Chinese refineries, running at 75% of capacity, hold the spare capacity that could relieve the squeeze.
